title: Competitive gap capture for niche-domain models and procurement triggers
creator: Aria Chen
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable system and playbook that surfaces gaps in the model ecosystem for narrow / regulated verticals (legal, healthcare, finserv niche models) and translates signals into procurement triggers for Dedicated/Private capacity.

Background: Many enterprise customers require specialized behavior (compliance-aware responses, medical terminology, jurisdictional grounding) where mainstream open models degrade. Sales and Solutions teams raise a steady stream of ad hoc requests for model variants; Ops lacks a reliable signal pipeline to prioritize procurement or onboarding work. This ticket scopes a lightweight heuristics layer plus an actionable trigger matrix for procurement and sourcing.

Scope & Deliverables:
- Signal taxonomy: list and normalize signals (latency/price delta, API behavior diffs, license incompatibility, tokenizer drift on domain corpora, hallucination rate on domain prompts).
- Scoring heuristic: prototype a 0-100 gap score for (region, vertical, capability) using weighted signals.
- Procurement trigger matrix: map score buckets to recommended actions (hosted routing adjustments, model onboarding, reserved capacity procurement, legal review).
- Dashboard prototype: a single-pane view for PMs/Sales/Solutions showing top 25 gaps, per-customer exposure, and recommended action.
- Runbook: concise operational steps and owners for each trigger (who to call, timelines, and rollback guidance).

Out-of-scope: full automation of procurement (this ticket produces signals and recommended actions only). Deep model evaluation pipeline (will integrate to separate evaluation infra work).

Success metrics:
- First 3 enterprise customer signals converted into procurement discussions within 3 weeks of alert.
- Dashboard showing >= 80% accuracy in prioritizing the top 10 customer-impact gaps as validated by Solutions interviews.
- Time-to-action (from signal to defined next-step) reduced from baseline ~21 days to <=10 days for high-priority gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy documented and validated by 4 PM/SE interviews
Scoring heuristic implemented as a reproducible notebook and linked in artifacts
Dashboard prototype with drilldowns available in staging Grafana and accessible to Solutions team
Procurement trigger matrix reviewed and approved by Legal and Procurement leads
Runbook with owners and SLAs published in Confluence

notes: Trade-offs: sampling-based tokenizer drift reduces cpu cost but may miss low-frequency customer prompts; plan to surface sampling confidence in dashboard.
Manual review vs automation: early phase will rely on human-in-the-loop validation before any procurement commit decisions.
Cost consideration: adding continuous drift scoring for all customers could add ~2-3% infra spend; prioritize customers with contractual SLAs when scaling.
Integration plan: scoring outputs will be an ingestable CSV/JSON that can be consumed by Watchtower and the Procurement Ops playbook.
